page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.48xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8559C processors using the x86_64 architecture. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The processor includes 320 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

This instance is characterized by its massive local storage capacity, bundling 120,000 GB of NVMe SSD storage. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. No graphics processing units are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests, alongside top-tier memory bandwidth for both small and large block read and write operations. Single-core performance is moderate, placing in the average tier for stress-ng single-core tests, though Geekbench single-core scores reach the top tier. The hardware demonstrates top-tier efficiency in database operations, Redis SET operations achieving 203.2 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput. It also shows strong to top-tier performance in LLM inference tasks, particularly for prompt processing on large 70B models.

Given the high density of both DDR5 memory and local NVMe SSD storage, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive local data retention alongside high-throughput memory access. The primary trade-off is the moderate single-core performance compared to its top-tier multi-core capabilities. It is suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, high-throughput Redis caching layers, data warehousing, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
